hero.headline: Your audience just became a craft critic
hero.sub: A dome in Inglewood restaged a 25-year-old film, SIGGRAPH moved photoreal capture into standard pipelines, and the internet torched a too-smooth ogre. One lesson across all three: surfaces are strategy now.
hero.statement: Your audience just became a craft critic.

sections.headline: Cosm turned a 25-year-old film into a venue-scale premiere
sections.body: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone in Shared Reality opened at Cosm Los Angeles in May: Warner Bros., Little Cinema, and MakeMake adapted the film so Hogwarts spills past the frame and onto the dome. The read for producers: IP holders now budget for staging, not screening. Catalog titles are experiential inventory.
sections.statement: Harry Potter didn't reopen a movie. It opened a room.
sections.why: Catalog IP is experiential inventory now.

sections.headline: Gaussian splatting graduated from demo to pipeline
sections.body: Out of SIGGRAPH 2026: OpenUSD v26.03 now includes a Gaussian splat schema, and a Filmakademie short ran a bedroom captured from 4,000 photos in real time inside Unreal. Photoreal location capture travels through standard tools — scan the venue, previz the activation, reuse the asset.
sections.statement: Photoreal capture walked out of the demo and into the pipeline.
sections.why: Scan the venue, previz the activation, reuse the asset.

sections.headline: Shrek got smoother. The audience called it fake.
sections.body: The June Shrek 5 teaser drew backlash sharp enough that comments got switched off. The craft problem isn't nostalgia; it's texture. Sand the grime and weight off a character and it reads synthetic — audiences now call that "AI slop." Polish isn't finish.
sections.statement: They sanded the grime off Shrek. The audience called it fake.

video.headline: A room becomes a splat
video.body: Sixty seconds on photoreal capture: from 4,000 stills to a real-time environment you can walk a camera through. The technique behind this month's pipeline shift, shown, not explained.
video.statement: Watch a room become a splat.

invitation.body: If a pitch on your desk needs real-time 3D, projection, or AR under your own brand, that's the layer we build. Reply.

teardown.statement: They sanded the grime off Shrek. The audience called it fake.
teardown.verdict: The June teaser drew backlash sharp enough that comments got switched off. It wasn't nostalgia. It was texture.
teardown.flaw: Sand the grime, pores and weight off a character and the eye clocks it instantly - it reads synthetic. The internet has a name for that now: "AI slop." The redesign chased clean and lost the hand-made friction that made the original feel alive.
teardown.principle: Polish and finish are not the same thing. Finish is the deliberate roughness that tells your senses something is real - the scuff, the fingerprint, the imperfect edge. Remove it and you remove belief.

done_right.label: Cosm LA
done_right.text: Same month, a dome in Inglewood restaged Harry Potter in shared reality - and kept every texture: dust in the light, weight in the stone. The surface did the convincing. That's the difference between rendering an image and rendering a place.
